issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking relief for the administration of a public religious or charitable trust cannot proceed when no breach of trust is proved and no directions for administration are sought.
material_facts: The plaintiffs brought a trust-management suit alleging misconduct and breach of trust by the person managing the institution and seeking his removal, accounts, and a management scheme.
The courts concurrently found that the alleged misconduct and breach of trust were not proved.
The plaintiffs did not claim that directions were necessary for the proper administration of the trust.
issues.conclusion: The foundation for a suit of this kind was absent, and the plaintiffs had no cause of action for the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 92 of the Civil Procedure Code, a suit of this special character presupposes a public religious or charitable trust and can proceed only where a breach of trust is alleged or directions are necessary for its administration, and the plaintiff seeks one or more of the reliefs specified in that section.

predicates.special_public_trust_management_suit: The plaintiffs brought a special suit seeking relief concerning the management of an alleged public religious or charitable trust.
predicates.trust_breach_not_proved: The courts found that the alleged breach of trust was not established.
predicates.administration_directions_not_sought: The plaintiffs did not claim that directions were needed for the proper administration of the trust.

issues.definition: When a special suit seeking management relief for an alleged public trust has neither a proved breach nor a request for administrative directions, the suit lacks a cause of action.

issues.legal_issue: A bare declaration that property belongs to a public trust cannot be granted as final relief in a special trust-management suit after the claims that could sustain that suit have failed.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought a declaration that the institution’s properties were trust properties, along with removal of the manager, accounts, and a management scheme.
The courts found that the alleged breach of trust was not proved, and the plaintiffs did not seek directions for the trust’s proper administration.
Although the suit was dismissed, the lower courts made the dismissal subject to a declaration that the properties belonged to a public religious and charitable trust.
issues.conclusion: The declaration was inconsequential and could not form part of the decree; the decree was modified to dismiss the suit without that declaration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 92 of the Civil Procedure Code permits only the reliefs specified in it. A declaration that property belongs to a trust may be available under general law, but it is outside the scope of section 92; it may be ancillary to a main relief under that section when the plaintiff is entitled to that relief. Abdur Rahim v. Barkat Ali (1928) 55 I.A. 96 supports the distinction between a declaration under general law and relief within section 92.

rule.if: special_public_trust_management_suit and trust_breach_not_proved and administration_directions_not_sought and main_trust_management_relief_unavailable
